glosses: to capitulate
капитулировать
poddawać się wrogowi poprzez zaniechanie walk i ustalanie, a potem podpisanie warunków poddania się
odstępować od swoich planów z powodu trudności
To surrender on stipulated terms, end all resistance, give up, go along with or comply.

examples.text: He argued and hollered for so long that I finally capitulated just to make him stop.
The Irish, after holding out a week, capitulated.
The CCP has refused to capitulate to Trump’s demands to come to the table and renegotiate their terms of trade.

glosses: To draw up in chapters, heads or articles; to enumerate, specify.

examples.text: The lawes […] which we capitulate at sea […] are not used on lande.
The places of serpents abode being thus generally capitulated.

glosses: To draw up articles of agreement with; to propose terms, treat, bargain, parley.

examples.text: there capitulates with the king […] to take to wife his daughter Mary

glosses: To make conditions, stipulate, agree, formulate, conclude (upon something).
Capitulated: agreed upon, convened, settled on, stipulated.

examples.text: It was capitulate and convenanted, that […] the river Himera, […]

glosses: Reduced to heads, laid down under a certain number of heads or items.
Having or forming a capitulum.

examples.text: The aggregation of flowers into capitulate inflorescences is a character directly advantageous from the aspect of the biological function of cross-pollination.

glosses: Alternative form of capitoulate
einen Kampf aufgeben, die eigene Niederlage eingestehen

examples.text: Diese Aufgabe ist zu schwierig für mich. Ich muss leider kapitulieren.
Erst als die Rebellen von der Armee umstellt waren, kapitulierten sie.
„Nach gut zweieinhalb Jahren kapitulieren die Buren am 31. Mai 1902.“
